audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Trundle all seven stages in a matchup Sejuani wins, with full.diff already labelled FAV — the chart and the label contradicted each other outright.
audit.why: The mirror audit at audits/top/trundle__sejuani.json already set his page to Trundle / Trundle / Skill / Skill / Sejuani / Sejuani / Sejuani. My side must state the same stages or mirror-fix will overwrite one of us.
audit.corrected: Stages 3 and 4-5 set to Skill; level 6, first item and two items set to Sejuani, matching the mirror exactly.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid gives Subjugate a '110 seconds base' cooldown and whys[4] gives Glacial Prison 900 range. Chomp carries no cooldown at all.
audit.why: Subjugate is 120/100/80 — 110 is not a rank at any point, so a player counting 110 commits ten seconds early at rank 1. Glacial Prison is 1300, not 900. Chomp is a flat 3.5 seconds, which is the number that explains why every short trade goes his way.
audit.corrected: Subjugate written as 120s at rank 1, Glacial Prison as 1300, Chomp as 3.5 seconds in whys[0], spikes[0] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] tells the player to dodge 'into his Pillar rather than away'.
audit.why: Pillar of Ice becomes impassable terrain — you cannot dash into it, and Arctic Assault into a pillar simply stops. The usable rule is the opposite one: the pillar is 21 seconds at rank 1 and its job is to seal the lane your Q would escape down, so position where it cannot cut you off.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around the pillar as terrain that seals your escape lane, with its 21-second cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Frost Armor's slow immunity is never mentioned, and Chomp being an auto-attack reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: Both of Trundle's slows — Chomp and Pillar of Ice — do nothing to an out-of-combat Sejuani while Frost Armor holds, which is the one structural edge she has in this lane. And Chomp resets his auto: the wind-up is the tell, not the cast, so stepping back on the cast is already too late.
audit.corrected: Slow immunity written into whys[3]; the reset wind-up written into whys[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds timing against King's Tribute and Frozen Domain.
audit.why: King's Tribute heals him off every nearby unit death and Frozen Domain increases healing he receives from all sources, so an un-shredded Trundle out-sustains your entire Frost loop.

audit.whatIsWrong: late claims Subjugate steals '20%' of your resistances.
audit.why: Riot's text gives no percentage — it says a percent of health, armour and magic resist, doubled over four seconds. Printing a made-up number is worse than printing none.
audit.corrected: Number removed; the doubling over four seconds stated instead, plus the real consequence that he wants to ult you while Frost Armor is full.

edits.after: Chomp is 3.5 seconds, resets his auto and saps your attack damage — the wind-up is the tell, so W the wave and last-hit at max range.
edits.before: Trundle Q bites on the first auto and steals your attack damage — no autos, no trades, W the wave and last-hit at max range.

edits.after: Frost Armor makes you immune to Chomp's slow and the pillar's while it holds, but extended trades still favour his healing — keep every exchange short and leave.
edits.before: Neither of you has a defining power tool — Trundle has sustain from Chomp, you have Frost stacks, and extended trades still favor his healing; respect it.

edits.after: Glacial Prison online means you open a trade before Subjugate applies — one R at 1300 range bypasses his entire early-lane damage advantage.
edits.before: Glacial Prison online means you can open a trade before Subjugate applies — one R at 900 range bypasses his entire early-lane damage advantage.

edits.after: Trundle's Chomp is 3.5 seconds and saps your attack damage on the reset — he wins every short trade before Frost can build.
edits.before: Trundle's Q bite steals your attack damage the moment he hits you — he wins every short trade before your Frost stacks can build.

edits.after: Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain on 21 seconds — stand where it cannot seal the lane your Arctic Assault escapes down
edits.before: Use Arctic Assault angle to dodge into his Pillar rather than away — stepping into it walls him, stepping away is what he wants

edits.after: Pop Subjugate while your Frost Armor is full so he steals the largest armour and magic resist pool you will ever carry
edits.before: Pop Subjugate the moment you commit an R or E stun so he drains your armor and magic resist at the exact window you need them

edits.after: Level 6 is your hard swing. Before Subjugate, Trundle is a beefy melee with a pillar and a slow zone — after it, he drains a percent of your resistances and you become a paper tank. The trade pattern: bait Chomp, which is up every 3.5 seconds, with a W-first approach, apply both Frost strikes, then E-stun him and back out or commit with R if your jungler is near. Never let Glacial Prison sit on cooldown while Trundle is on the short side of the wave — that is your invitation to start a pick. Subjugate is 120 seconds at rank 1: if it is down, full-commit; if it is up, fish for R and disengage after the stun.
edits.before: Level 6 is your hard swing. Before Subjugate, Trundle is a beefy melee with a pillar and a slow zone — after it, he's draining a percentage of your resistances and you become a paper tank. The trade pattern is: bait his Q bite with a W-first approach, apply both Frost strikes, then E-stun him and back out or commit with R if jungle is nearby. Never let Glacial Prison sit on cooldown when Trundle is on the short side of the wave — that's your invitation to start a pick. Track his Subjugate cooldown (110 seconds base); if it's down, you can full-commit; if it's up, fish for R and disengage after the stun.

edits.after: At two items Subjugate still steals a percent of your health and resistances and doubles it over four seconds, so he wants to ult you at your fattest — never open a fight fresh out of combat with Frost Armor full. Bring Grievous Wounds: King's Tribute heals him off every nearby death and Frozen Domain raises all the healing he receives. In teamfights he wants to steal from you and sit on a carry; deny it with Arctic Assault to re-engage after he commits R, and hold Permafrost for the step onto your backline. A Trundle who cannot reach a high-armour target is a melee with a slow and a pillar.
edits.before: At two items your base resistances are high enough that Subjugate's percentage drain hurts less in proportion — he's stealing 20% of a much larger pool but you regenerate it faster through Sunfire and Heartsteel's HP scaling. In teamfights, Trundle wants to Subjugate your frontline tank (you) and sit on a carry; deny that by using Arctic Assault to re-engage him after he commits his R, keeping your E stun for the moment he steps onto your backline. A Trundle who cannot reach a high-armor target is just a melee with a slow cone and a pillar — your W slow plus a well-angled Arctic Assault kite him into your team's damage instead.

notes: Two printed numbers were simply wrong: Subjugate given as '110 seconds base' when it is 120/100/80, and Glacial Prison given as 900 range when it is 1300. A player counting 110 commits ten seconds early. Also removed a fabricated '20%' resistance-steal figure — Riot's text gives no percentage — and replaced the 'dodge into his Pillar' advice, which cannot be done because Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain. The interaction worth the most and entirely absent: Frost Armor grants slow immunity, so both of Trundle's slows do nothing to an out-of-combat Sejuani. Chart aligned to the mirror at audits/top/trundle__sejuani.json rather than to the disk, which gave Trundle all seven stages while the same file labelled the matchup FAV.
